props.gloss_en: the Rav / Rav Kahana dispute concerns whether an exactly-half-cut siman counts as a majority for slaughter
the Rav / Rav Kahana dispute was stated about the Paschal offering, where half the people were impure
for slaughter, a siman of which exactly half was cut is treated like one of which the majority was cut
for slaughter, a siman of which exactly half was cut is NOT treated like one of which the majority was cut
when exactly half the people are impure on the fourteenth of Nisan, their status is that of a majority: the whole people sacrifices in impurity
when exactly half the people are impure their status is NOT that of a majority: the pure sacrifice on the fourteenth, the impure on Pesach sheni
Rav's stated ground for the shechita-version: the Merciful One said to Moses 'do not leave a majority of the siman uncut'
Rav Kahana's stated ground for the shechita-version: the Merciful One said to Moses 'cut a majority'
Rav's ground in the Pesach case: 'any man who shall be impure' (Num 9:10) -- an individual is deferred to Pesach sheni, but a congregation is not deferred; half the people count as a congregation
our mishna: if one cut half of one siman in a bird, or one and a half simanim in an animal, his slaughter is not valid
the mishna's disqualification is rabbinic, lest he not come to cut even half -- so it does not refute Rav
an impure earthenware vessel divided into two seemingly equal halves -- both remain impure, because it is impossible to divide precisely (Rav Ketina's proof-text)
there are no two majorities in one vessel -- so exactly-half cannot count as a majority there, while for a single siman it can
one cut half the windpipe, paused the measure of another slaughter, and completed it -- his slaughter is valid
that baraita concerns a bird, which requires the cutting of only one siman -- which is what makes the mah nafshach at 29a.2 run
half the windpipe was deficient before slaughter, and the slaughterer added an incision of any size and completed it -- his slaughter is valid
Rava: for rendering an animal a tereifa, where a majority is required it must be a conspicuous majority (רוב הנראה לעינים)
for slaughter too a conspicuous majority is required -- Abaye's a-fortiori conclusion, incompatible with exactly-half counting as a majority

schemas.gloss_en: in a bird: if half is like a majority, the majority was already cut before the pause; if it is not, the half-cut was nothing and no tereifa arose -- either way the slaughter is valid

if tereifa, triggered by any minuscule deficiency, requires a conspicuous majority where a majority is required, then shechita, valid only once a majority is cut, surely requires a conspicuous majority
